resources.string: A qualitative view of normal oxygen delivery. Sizes, timing and oxygen symbols are not to scale and do not represent oxygen levels. The full circulation and carbon dioxide exchange are not shown. This is not medical advice.
A red blood cell is a disk with a dip on each side. Inside it, many hemoglobin molecules can reversibly bind oxygen. The inset shows one simplified hemoglobin molecule.
Oxygen diffuses from the air in an alveolus across the thin air–blood barrier. It enters red cells in a nearby lung capillary and binds to hemoglobin.
Blood flow carries red cells toward the tissues. Most oxygen in the blood travels bound to hemoglobin inside those cells.
Where less oxygen is dissolved in the blood, some oxygen separates from hemoglobin. It leaves the red cell and dissolves in the plasma.
Oxygen diffuses down its partial-pressure gradient: from blood across the capillary wall, through tissue fluid and into nearby cells. Red cells stay inside the vessel.
Colburn et al. (2020): Oxygen gradients across muscle capillaries
